children: According to CNBC, Westwood Holdings Group CEO Brian Casey said he is bullish on the Texas Stock Exchange and pointed to Dallas's growing role as a corporate hub, citing the city's central location, major airport access and Texas efforts to make incorporation easier and less expensive. Energy Transfer, Sunoco and Dillard's have recently said they will shift their listings from NYSE to TXSE, while Westwood launched the exchange's first new ETF, the Westwood Salient Enhanced Power & Infrastructure ETF, to invest across the power ecosystem from utilities to grid infrastructure and next-generation technologies. Casey also said the AI buildout will require more than $600 billion of investment over a 10-year period, with 50 gigawatts of power needed by 2030 for data centers and 2,000 gigawatts currently in the interconnection queue.

title: Westwood CEO Says Texas Stock Exchange, AI Power Demand Drive New ETF Launch
